text.p: Following are highlights of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Defence Minister Gojko Susak travels to the United States for his regular medical checkup and working meetings with Robert Gelbard, a special representative of the U.S. president Bill Clinton, and the Secretary of State Madeleine Albright as well as Defence Secretary William Cohen.
- The price of new flats to rise by up to 10 percent from January 1998 due to the introduction of VAT.
- More than 30,000 vehicles are currently passing through Karlovac each day as the tourist season peak nears.
- British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook accuses the Bosnia-Herzegovina leadership of corruption and appropriating a large part of foreign financial assistance.
- The work of the central bank described by Finance Minister Bozo Prka as very good. Prka says that the bank fulfilled its two main tasks: maintaining the stability of the kuna and liquidity.
- We want to lure Danish tourists back to the Croatian coast, Croatian ambassador to Denmark Marijo Nikolic says in an interview.
- An average of 14 hours' train delays in both domestic and international travel are recorded at Zagreb's train station every day.
- Changes to the penal code bring about the possiblity of rapists getting up to a 15-year sentence.

- President of the Bosnian Federation Vladimir Soljic, who at the same time presides over the newly founded Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, says the Croats look up to Jewish communities all over the world as role models.
- Wife of the Croatian Tourism Minister Niko Bulic wins an award in the competition for the new tourist slogan: Croatia - Heaven On Earth.
- Most of the Croatian Serbs returning to the Knin region claim they come back for the sake of their homes and to collect state pensions.
- Fish products trader Vigo Company buys 29.45 percent of the Split-based fishery Jadranribolov to complete its takeover. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
